Koko joined a walking group and picked up the pace. Now the front of her shins aches whenever she walks faster.

caption:
Toto spent three hours on a picnic rug in the park. Every time he stood up, his back ached and his legs felt tingly.

Staying in one position on the ground for a long time can leave your back and hips feeling stiff. Raising your hips a little on a folded towel or cushion, and changing position every 15–20 minutes, can make it easier.

Hybi's tips: lean back on a tree or a bag, and kneel first before stepping up to stand. Stop if leg tingling lingers or pain gets worse.

caption:
For Lulu, lifting his toddler into the car seat is harder than anything on site. Every twist and reach gives his back a twinge.

The further you reach, and the more you twist while holding a load, the harder your back works. Face the car seat, hold your toddler close, and turn with your feet rather than your back.

Hybi's tips: open the door wide, put one knee on the back seat to get closer, and if your little one can walk, let them climb in themselves.
